title: Per-atom latency & KV-delta attribution ledger with streaming trace hooks
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build an instrumentation layer that emits per-atom (subtoken/wordpiece) timing events, attributes latency and marginal cost to KV-cache delta behavior, and exposes streaming trace hooks to the observability pipeline. Background: downstream billing and SLA dashboards need a clear, explainable mapping from request-level latency/cost to the underlying emission stages (embedding lookups, attention kernel, KV fetch/hits, tokenizer emission). Current telemetry aggregates at request or sequence level which obscures cache effects and makes proactive optimizations (prefetching, batching policy changes) hard to quantify. Scope: 1) Define a compact per-atom event schema suitable for both sampling and full-stream capture. 2) Instrument runtime emission pipeline to emit events with step timings, KV request/response markers, cache hit/miss flags, and KV-delta bytes. 3) Implement an in-service micro-aggregator that converts high-frequency atom events into time-windowed rollups for metrics ingestion and a separate low-sample full-stream sink for traces. 4) Add transformation logic to compute marginal token latency and marginal cost credited (or debited) to cache hits/misses and prefetch behavior. 5) Wire outputs into our metrics + logs pipeline (Prometheus-compatible histograms, OTLP traces, and kafka event stream for billing ledger).
acceptance_criteria: Per-atom event schema reviewed and approved by Observability and Runtime teams
Runtime emits per-atom events with stable schema and <=2% p99 overhead under benchmark traffic
Micro-aggregator produces windowed histograms and KV-delta counters that match sampled ground-truth within 3%
OTLP traces include atom-level spans and a KV-delta span that can be linked to request-level trace
Dashboards updated: token-latency waterfall, cache-delta heatmap, and per-route cost attribution visible in Console
Documentation and migration notes for downstream billing consumers provided
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with runtime and observability. Agreed on using OTLP + kafka hybrid sink. Decided schema must be stable for 6 months.
2026-02-20: Prototype per-atom emitter implemented behind feature flag. Initial tests show ~1.6% median CPU increase and p95 latency +0.9% on a 4k sequence benchmark.

2026-02-25: Design review notes from SRE: insist on size-bounded atom events and a sampling header to avoid unbounded trace volume. Action: add 'sample_reason' and 'sample_rate' fields and enforce 64KB per-request event budget.
2026-03-01: Implemented micro-aggregator in observability service. Aggregator performs 500ms tumbling windows, outputs Prometheus histograms and kafka ledger records keyed by route+model+cache_key.

2026-03-03: QA run with synthetic burst traffic. Observed mismatch between aggregator KV-delta sums and sampled trace sums (~7% delta). Root cause: double-counting prefetch responses when re-used across simultaneous requests. Workaround: de-duplicate KV IDs at aggregator level; next step: add per-prefetch id in emitter.

2026-03-05: Code change to emit prefetch_id and kv_request_id landed (PR referenced). Integration tests passing locally. Scheduling rollout to staging on 2026-03-07 behind the feature flag 'per_atom_attrib_v1'.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full-stream capture provides perfect attribution but is heavy; decided for hybrid approach (sampled full-stream + deterministic rollups) to balance accuracy and cost.
Potential follow-ups: adaptive sampling tied to surge detection, per-customer sampling rates for enterprise tiers, and exposing per-customer cache-credit metrics to billing.
Instrumentation must include tokenizer boundary markers so we can attribute multi-byte UTF-8 grapheme clusters correctly for non-English workloads.
Need to coordinate with Billing team to map KV-delta bytes to dollar cost before GA. Assigned owner: Priya Bhandari (Billing).
Ops requirement: aggregator should expose a 'reconcile' endpoint that compares recent windowed sums to sampled trace sums for drift detection.
